Vancouver Storm #1

Behind The Net

Stephanie Archer

3.77
218,752 ratings20,684 reviews
Rate this book
He's the hot, grumpy goalie I had a crush on in high school... and now I'm his live-in assistant.

After my ex crushed my dreams in the music industry, I’m done with getting my heart broken. Working as an assistant for an NHL player was supposed to be a breeze, but nothing about Jamie Streicher is easy. He’s an intimidatingly hot, grouchy jerk who can't stand me. The guy has a massive ego. Keeping things professional will be no problem, even when he demands I move in with him.


Beneath his surliness, though, Jamie’s surprisingly sweet and protective.

When Jamie learns how bad my ex was in bed, his competitive nature flares, and he encourages and spoils me in every way. The creative spark I used to feel about songwriting? It’s back, and I’m writing music again. Between wearing his jersey at games, rowdy parties with the team, and being brave on stage again, I’m falling for him.

He could break my heart, but it might be worth it.

Behind the Net is a grumpy-sunshine pro hockey romance with lots of spice and an HEA. It’s the first book in the Vancouver Storm series, and can be read as a standalone.

Tropes:

- grumpy sunshine
- slow burn
- boy obsessed
- pro hockey
- forced proximity (boss vs assistant + roommates)
- spice coaching

“He looks at me like there are a thousand kind, loving things he wants to say.”

Now I'm gonna be real with you and tell you that the only reason I read this book was so I can read the second book because that is what I've been wanting, but honestly, this was such a nice surprise?!? I loved how fluffy and cute this was. This can be considered cringey and cheesy at times, but I honestly don't care because I think this is exactly what I needed to get out of my slump!! The chapters were short, and the writing complemented the pacing. Reading during exam seasons with a slump can be very exhausting, and I think that is why I'm not getting out of my slump, because to pick up a book in that environment is so stressful that it doesn't quite grip my attention, but this excels at that, it created this comforting atmosphere which is what I needed to subtly escape my slump.

The characters Jamie and Pippa were cute characters but honestly I only liked them because they were together, if I look at them as separate character I know I wont like them that much, like don't get me wrong I liked the development that we got regarding their characters but I just feel like they were just not interesting enough. Moving on, the romance, on a normal day, I would not enjoy something that has this level of insta-lust, because it's not my cup of my tea but i feel like I was just so desperate to enjoy a book and I was enjoying this so it didn't affect me, I liked the sweet domestic moment they got and the spice was phenomenal so hehe cant wait for the next book.

Overall, a nice palette cleanser!

this is probably gonna be a very short review, because i don’t have that much to say i know, i was shocked too. plus i also want to give myself a break and not force reviews on books where i actually don’t have that much to say, because those reviews don't make me happy and most of it is just words and i'm just trying to fill out the review, but you’ll no longer be seeing me do that. now i just wanna enjoy my reading and enjoy writing reviews (there will still be rants, love letters, long reviews etc. just not from books where i actually don’t have that much to say)

this is just a regular hockey romance book and hockey romances will always hit one way or another. this was surprisingly good, but again nothing special. i did enjoy this because all i needed was a hockey romance with a little spice and spice i definitely got, but if you’re looking for something more and deeper than that this book won’t satisfy you, but i’d still recommend if you’re in the mood for a cute, spicy, easy read. normally i’d write a paragraph about each main character, but as i said i don’t have that much to say. the characters were likeable and cute together, but it wasn’t any of those characters you’ll remember for the rest of your life, but that’s good too sometimes, they can’t all be nesta archeron's and dante maroni’s. when that’s said i would’ve liked the book more if he didn’t call her “my pretty assistant” every second chapter, but i’m willing to overlook that a little because i’ve been in a big ass slump and i finished this book so that means it must’ve done something right. i’m also really looking forward to the second book in this series, because i already know that bantering is gonna be great and i love the characters. i honestly think it’s time for me to get back into my hockey romance era, because i’ve missed these vibes so much.

⊹ ࣪ ˖ "something has shifted in my chest, locked into place. this is right. this is the way it's supposed to be. i thought about her all those years, and we found our way back to each other.


₊ ⊹ to start, i want to say thank you to my gorgeous bsf giu for reading this book with me. you truly just get me, and getting to laugh over this book with you was such a fun time. i love you forever and i can't wait to read the rest of this series with you. you're the hazel to my pippa ♡♡

┆ ⤿ ⛸️ ⌗ thoughts
⟡ i really didn't have the highest expectations for this one because of all the bad reviews, so i can't even say i'm surprised. in fact, i had such low expectations that i was able to enjoy some aspects of this book! it was annoying, cringe, and very...smutty at times. but i also was able to enjoy some other aspects of it.

let's start with what i enjoyed.
⟡ for one, i really love singers in books (which i know is an unpopular opinion). maybe it's the fact that i'm so in love with music, singers, and lyrics, so whenever i read a book focused around a singer it makes me happy. as long as it's done right, and in this case, i think it was. pippa was such a cutie on stage, and getting to see her step out of her comfort zone and perform again was really fun to watch. the lyrics didn't need to be mentioned though, because those were atrocious.

⟡ also, i loved jamie's teammates. hayden, volkov, and rory were all so entertaining and fun. i can already tell that, while i didn't particularly love this book, i'm going to love the other ones (or so i'm hoping, since i bought the entire series beforehand...) hayden was such a golden boy, and i loved the way he just radiated sunshine and happiness. boys like those are my favorite, where they are just carefree and can have a good time. rory was so mean at first, and i immediately didn't like him, but he's grown on me. i can tell he really has a big heart, he just doesn't get along well with jamie (which... i don't blame him). he was also really cute with pippa, and i loved their friendship. i don't know much about volkov yet, but i always love those quiet, older men in books, so i already know i'm going to like him.

⟡ i loved how he was in love with her since high school, and the fact that she was a band kid.

⟡ NO THIRD-ACT BREAKUP!!! i think that says enough on it's own.

here are the things i didn't enjoy.
⟡ the cringey nickname. "songbird" is terrible, especially coming from a man whose whole thing is to be "possessive" and "brooding". and okay, maybe in theory it's not all that bad. but his inner monologue saying 'the pretty songbird' no. LEAVE RIGHT NOW.

⟡ i hated how dragged out the end was. a HOCKEY ROMANCE book does not have any right being almost 400 pages. the last 20% really felt like pulling teeth, and i had to push through to get it done.

⟡ the smut. what do you mean he sent her a sex toy when he was drunk, and then she was using it??!! also i just hated how it immediately turned from 'i've been in love with you since highschool' turned to 'she looks so fuckable'. COME AWNNNN.

┆ ⤿🌷 ⌗ characters

⋮ ⌗ ┆ pippa
surprisingly enough, i thought she was cute! like i said, i loved the singer aspect and her learning to forget the negative stuff people have said about her so she can live happily. i also think she was an angel for putting up with some of jamie's shit, cause i could never!

the epilogue made me so happy for her, i'm glad she's finally living her dream of being a singer <3

⋮ ⌗ ┆ jamie
can we please burn all nonchalant men?? when he met her for the first time since high school, he was shocked to see her at his front door saying she was going to be his agent. and instead of being nice or flirting (LITERALLY ANYTHING) he decides to treat her like garbage. because he...likes her still? how does that add up. genuinely.

and his whole "possessive" thing wasn't really cute, it was just annoying. i don't blame miller for not liking him, because he was just an asshole to everyone! even when hayden, the sunshine boy who is friends with everyone, would talk to pippa, jamie would be sending threatening glares towards him and being snappy. i PROMISE he doesn't want your girl, he's literally like that with everyone.

⋮ ⌗ ┆ jamie + pippa
their story was going so good, with the tension and everything, and then all of a sudden it just went away? and they were immediately just boyfriend/girlfriend. there was no "what are we?" talk, nothing like that. and then all of a sudden they were fiances. i think that could've been worked through more.

i love how pippa was so in love with jamie, even though she deserves better. and jamie really did support pippa's music career wholeheartedly, which i adored. he was her biggest cheerleader and not once didn't believe in her. :')

┆ ⤿ 🎧 ⌗ final thoughts

to sum up my thoughts on this book : ( in the wise words of giu ) "daisy (the fucking dog) was the best character"

can't wait for the rest of the series though, cause i know it's gonna eat

3.75 stars

“Pippa Hartley is standing in my living room, playing with the dog, and I can’t breathe.”


Behind the Net has everything I was craving in a good sports romance—a grumpy hockey player, the cutest dog, a perfect balance of romance and sports, wholesome moments, and immaculate spice. The story wasn’t anything special, just a typical hockey romance, yet I devoured it in just two days. It’s a bit long for a contemporary romance, but I have no idea where those 440 pages flew by. The pacing was slow—it’s a slow burn, given the fact that the characters had instant attraction to each other—but the insta-lust/love was executed so well.

This is my first book by Stephanie Archer, and I can see myself getting used to her writing, her characters, and especially her sweet and spicy stories. The writing was simple, the characters were drawn out viscerally, with depth and vulnerability that made them feel real and flawed. The spice in this book is one of the best I’ve read in a while! It was so good!

“I thought you were gorgeous, too,” he murmurs, looking at me in a way that makes me feel like I can’t breathe. “Even back then.”


Pippa Hartley had been betrayed by her ex-boyfriend, he stole her confidence, faith, and trust. She is an incredible singer but struggles with musical creativity until Jamie walks into her life and makes her see how incredible she is. Pippa is a hard-working woman who feels deeply and is the sweetest person. She is thoughtful and kind, but there is a fire within her that only Jamie can bring out. I liked seeing her growth—from a girl with no dreams to one with passion, bringing out the real Pippa.

“I sing my heart out. I sing about wanting more, wanting to believe in myself, wanting to break free and be my own person.”


Jamie Streicher is the grumpy striker—the one who hates everyone but loves his dog and his girl, Pippa. He carries the burden of everything in his life and wants to make things right because he feels obliged to everyone around him. It took me a while to warm up to his character because he was unnecessarily rude at times, but once he started showing his sweet and loving side—the one that cares for the people he loves—I couldn’t help but swoon over him. He was also possessive when it came to Pippa, and we love a jealous man.

“Pippa’s my forever person.”

“I love coming home to you.”

“She smiles, and I fall a little harder for her.”


Pippa and Jamie’s love story is filled with wholesomeness, sweetness, witty banter, emotional moments, and the perfect amount of spice. Their obsession with each other runs deep—their chemistry is sizzling, heavy with sexual tension and undeniable attraction. What I truly loved was how they helped each other and found comfort in each other’s company. How Jamie helped Pippa regain her confidence, how he pushed her to create music just for herself because he loved her in every way. And how Pippa made sure Jamie never felt alone, always giving him her support and love. It was simply so beautiful and precious.

“You need to stop looking at me like that, songbird”
“Or what?”
“Or I’m going to lose my mind.”


This book has no third-act breakup or miscommunication trope, and the ending was perfect and satisfying. I’m so excited for Rory and Hazel’s story next. I have a feeling it’s going to be my favourite in this series!

———————
Just need a cute and no brainer hockey romance 😗
